data.abstract: Power transformers are among the most critical assets in power systems, and their reliability directly affects system stability and operational efficiency. A major factor limiting transformer life is thermal aging of insulation, which is strongly influenced by hot-spot temperature, harmonic distortion, and load-induced losses. Excessive heating caused by these factors accelerates deterioration and shortens service duration. While much of the existing research emphasizes condition monitoring and predictive life estimation, fewer studies address direct mitigation of thermal stress through design improvements. In this work, a series compensator is proposed on both the primary and secondary sides of the transformer to minimize harmonic currents and regulate loading effects. Simulation analysis demonstrates that the design results in a noticeable reduction in transformer loss of life percentage. The findings suggest that compensator-based interventions can extend thermal life expectancy, enhance operational reliability, and support sustainable asset management of power transformers.

data.abstract: This paper presents a detailed case study on the estimation of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of oil-filled power transformers that have been in continuous service for periods ranging from 20 to 54 years. The ageing of transformers is primarily governed by the deterioration of their solid insulation, and accurate prediction of residual life is essential for ensuring grid reliability, planning maintenance, and avoiding costly failures. While thermal ageing laws such as the Arrhenius model have been traditionally employed, they often oversimplify ageing by considering temperature as the sole factor. In this study, particular emphasis is placed on chemical-based diagnostics, specifically Furan analysis, which provides insight into cellulose degradation, and the Degree of Polymerization (DP), which serves as a direct indicator of paper mechanical strength. Data from 16 operational transformers were collected and analyzed, and life estimation was performed using established empirical relationships. The findings reveal that several units still retain significant service potential beyond their nominal design life, demonstrating the practical value of DP and Furan analysis in condition-based life assessment and strategic asset management.

data.abstract: Accurate prediction of the internal temperature is significant for assessing the operating status and remaining life of the oil-immersed transformer. In this study, a two-dimensional closed-loop simulation model of thermal-flow field for a 110-kV power transformer with the oil natural/air forced cooling mode is developed to predict the temperature distribution. The influence of eddy current loss, loss distribution and loss temperature effect on temperature distribution of transformer are compared and analyzed. The results showed that the ignorance of eddy loss makes the temperature of the high-voltage winding and the low-voltage winding decrease in the simulation, and the hot-spot temperature decreases by 3.44 °C. The loss distribution mainly affects the temperature at the top of high-voltage winding and the bottom of low-voltage winding, and the influence is insignificant. The temperature effect of loss is indispensable to be considered in the simulation as it is difficult to accurately estimate the reference temperature used in the calculation of loss. It is found that the loss loading mode has negligible effect on the location of the hot-spot temperature.

data.abstract: Transformers are increasingly being subjected to dynamic, non-linear loading profiles driven by the stochastic nature of renewable energy integration and the high power demands of electric vehicle charging infrastructure. The primary limiting factor of transformer lifespan is the thermal degradation of its solid insulation system, typically oil impregnated cellulose. Precise real time Hot-Spot Temperature (HST) estimation is therefore critical for transformer reliability, for which traditional numerical methods are computationally prohibitive while standard data-driven models lack physical consistency. This paper proposes a novel hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework that integrates the governing transient heat diffusion partial differential equations (PDEs) directly into the deep learning architecture. The model is integrated with the recommendations of IEEE standards to provide a continuous real-time estimate of the aging Acceleration Factor (FAA), enabling proactive monitoring of the insulation life of the transformer.
